summary: This project is an illustrated field guide to NASA hardware left on the Moon and Mars. We created two slide decks: a six-slide overview and a 36-slide detailed guide. The guide follows lunar experiments and the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, then explores Mars missions including Viking, Pathfinder and Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity, Phoenix, and InSight. Each section explains what the equipment was designed to do, how it operated on the surface, and what observations or discoveries it enabled. Using NASA mission records and imagery, the project addresses the challenge by connecting each artifact to its location, purpose, and scientific legacy. The guide makes planetary exploration easier for school-age readers and general audiences to follow.
details:
We created an illustrated field guide as two editable slide decks: a six-slide overview and a 36-slide detailed edition. Designed for school-age readers and general audiences, the guide pairs NASA surface imagery with clear explanations of equipment, mission purpose, surface operations, and scientific findings.

The Moon section covers Apollo surface experiments and the Lunar Roving Vehicle. The Mars section follows landers and rovers from Viking and Pathfinder/Sojourner to Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, and InSight. Other pages compare the Moon and Mars environments, explain why mission hardware can remain on a planetary surface, and distinguish observations from scientific interpretations.

The project’s educational benefit is to make planetary science more tangible by connecting hardware to the places it explored and the evidence it collected. We used NASA mission records and images, plus ChatGPT to help organize research, draft and edit explanatory text, and plan slide layouts. The final project is a presentation; it does not include an app, custom code, hardware, or video. No AI-generated images were used.
